issues.display_title: Issue #1544: Tour Transfer (With or Without Tour Key) Not Working Anymore
issues.main_description_html:
Description

The Transfer Tour feature is broken — transferring a tour with or without tour key no longer works.

From the Transfer Tour modal, the user enters a destination Email Address, clicks Transfer, and selects a transfer mode from the dropdown:

  • Keep the Tour IDs
  • Get New Tour IDs

Neither option currently completes the transfer successfully.

Impact

  • Users cannot transfer tours to another account.
  • Blocking a real request: a user has 20 tours to transfer and cannot do it in bulk (no manual workaround acceptable).

Scope to investigate

  • Reproduce the failure for both transfer modes: Keep the Tour IDs and Get New Tour IDs.
  • Check the tour transfer endpoint/handler on the API for errors (recent regression — "not working anymore").
  • Verify transfer works both with and without the tour key.
  • Review recent changes/deploys that may have broken the transfer flow.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Transferring a tour with Keep the Tour IDs succeeds — the tour appears under the destination email account with the same tour IDs.
  2. Transferring a tour with Get New Tour IDs succeeds — the tour appears under the destination account with newly generated IDs.
  3. Transfer works both with and without a tour key.
  4. Bulk transfer of multiple tours (e.g. the reporter's 20) works without manual intervention.

Debug Results

At the end of the transfer process. The "transfer" worker does not hit the /v2/tours/clone-overlay-after-transfer api.

I added a "start clone overlay after transfer" log as a marker that the API was hit but it is not there when the log file is opened.

issues.display_title: Issue #1605: Fix Bug Review Photographer Modal Displays Reviewer's Portfolio Instead of Applicant's
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A critical data-fetching issue has been reported in the Featured Photographers → Review Photographer modal.

When a Support/Admin user opens a photographer's profile for review and navigates to the "Portfolio" tab, the system incorrectly loads and displays the reviewer's own virtual tours (e.g., the admin's personal GoThru portfolio), rather than the tours belonging to the photographer being reviewed.

This prevents the Support team from properly evaluating the applicant's work before approving or denying them.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When opening the "Review Photographer" modal and navigating to the Portfolio tab, the system successfully fetches and displays the virtual tours belonging to that specific applicant.
  2. The reviewer's own personal virtual tours never appear in the portfolio list of another user.

Test Scenario (for Tester / QA)

Preconditions

  • Logged in as a Support/Admin account that itself has a non-empty GoThru portfolio (own virtual tours) — this is key to reproducing the bug.
  • At least one applicant photographer exists in Featured Photographers whose portfolio is different from the admin's (ideally with recognizable tour titles).

Scenario 1 — Applicant's portfolio loads (the bug)

  1. Go to Support → Featured Photographers.
  2. Open an applicant's Review Photographer modal.
  3. Click the Portfolio tab.
  4. ✅ Expected: The listed tours belong to the applicant (titles/links match the applicant's account), not the admin's own tours.
  5. ❌ Bug (before fix): The admin's own virtual tours are shown instead.

Scenario 2 — Cross-check different applicants

  1. Close the modal and open a different applicant's Review Photographer modal → Portfolio tab.
  2. ✅ Expected: The portfolio changes to that second applicant's tours. Two different applicants must never show the same (admin's) list.

Scenario 3 — Reviewer's own tours never leak

  1. Note the admin's own portfolio tour titles beforehand.
  2. Review several applicants' Portfolio tabs.
  3. ✅ Expected: The admin's own tours never appear in any applicant's portfolio list.

Scenario 4 — Applicant with empty portfolio

  1. Open the Review modal for an applicant who has no tours.
  2. ✅ Expected: An empty/no-tours state is shown — not the admin's tours as a fallback.

Scenario 5 — Switching tabs / reopening

  1. Within one applicant's modal, switch between tabs (Account Statistics / Profile / Location / Portfolio / Gear) and back to Portfolio; also close and reopen the modal.
  2. ✅ Expected: Portfolio consistently shows the correct applicant's tours every time (no stale data from a previous open or from the admin).

Pass criteria: Every applicant's Portfolio tab shows only that applicant's tours; the reviewer's own tours never appear for any other user.

Reference: docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md — see §3 Persona D (Support/Admin) and §4 (Photographer profile & directory).

issues.display_title: Issue #1659: Handle Issue Publish Status Page Stuck in Endless Loading State
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A user reported that the Publish Status page for a specific tour (https://app.gothru.co/my-tours/3503626/publish-status) is stuck in a continuous, endless loading loop.

According to the user, the underlying publishing pipeline seems to have worked correctly because all images under the "Edit" section are displaying as green (indicating successful processing/publishing). This suggests the issue is likely a frontend state resolution failure or an API response error that the UI is not handling gracefully.

"this page does not stop loading"
"I do not think the issue is from my publishing pipeline, since under Edit all images display green"

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The Publish Status page successfully resolves the loading state and accurately displays the tour's current status.
  2. If the API request fails or times out, the page gracefully handles the error and displays a readable error message to the user rather than an endless loading state.

Note from Developer

Root cause: GET /sv/moderation/{id}/map-approval was timing out with cURL error 28 after exactly 30 seconds.

The upstream service at 192.168.1.44:7827/v1/moderations/{id}/map-approval is inherently slow (response time >30s). Laravel's PendingRequest has a hardcoded default timeout: 30 in its options — skipping the ->timeout() call does not override this default. A prior fix (commit 42955ca35) only removed PHP's set_time_limit(), which removes the script execution limit but does not affect the HTTP client timeout.

Fix (commit 433fbcd9a): Added an optional $timeout parameter to StreetViewPublisherService::get() (default: 30s for all other endpoints). getMapApproval() now explicitly passes timeout=0, which overrides the PendingRequest default and tells Guzzle/cURL to wait indefinitely for the upstream response.

issues.display_title: Issue #1704: Endpoint to Set Portfolio Visibility — One Tour or the Whole Account
issues.main_description_html:
• Column written: not_public

Context

Nothing currently writes not_public. One endpoint covers both cases — ticking a single checkbox and Show All / Hide All. The frontend does not get a separate single-tour endpoint.

So the request needs two things: the direction (is_public true/false) and the target — either a set of tours, or the whole account.

The target must be explicit. An empty or missing tour list must never be treated as "everything" — that turns one frontend bug into a customer's entire portfolio going dark. Make "whole account" something the caller has to say on purpose, and reject a request that names no target at all.

Bulk must be one operation, not one per tour. An agency account with 500 tours has to work.

Note: editPortfolio (used by /portfolio/edit) writes a different flag, is_checked — leave it alone, that page is out of scope.

Where the data lives
Connection googlemaps — DatabaseClass::dbGoogleMaps()
Table google_plus — reached via DatabaseClass::tableGooglePlus()
Column to write not_public
Row identifier used by the frontend cid
Account scope user_id — every read and write must carry it

Values are compared as strings throughout the existing code — whereIn('not_public', ["0", ""]), $portfolio == true ? "1" : "0". Write strings, not integers or booleans, or the existing readers will miss the rows.

There is no migration for this table in the repo — it is a legacy schema. Check the live table before assuming a type, and don't add or alter columns as part of this issue. Nothing here needs a schema change; it writes a column that already exists.

For the all path, the update is a single statement scoped by user_id. Worth confirming user_id is indexed on google_plus before shipping — a 500-tour account is small, but this table holds every account's tours.

Proposed contract

Adjust the shape if something fits the codebase better — but keep scope explicit and keep is_public meaning the same thing it means in the list response.

POST /portfolios/panoramas/visibility

Single tour — what the checkbox sends:

{
  "is_public": false,
  "scope": "selected",
  "cids": ["1234567890123456789"]
}

Whole account — what Show All / Hide All sends:

{
  "is_public": true,
  "scope": "all"
}
Field Rules
is_public required, boolean. true writes not_public = "0", false writes "1"
scope required, one of selected | all
cids required when scope is selected, array, at least one entry. Ignored when scope is all

Response carries the same summary block the summary endpoint returns, so the frontend can refresh both counts without calling it again:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "messages": "...",
    "summary": {
      "total": 42,
      "total_public": 18
    }
  }
}

Case Result
scope missing, or selected with empty / absent cids 400, nothing written
cids containing tours that belong to another account not written — reject the request rather than silently skipping
no token / expired 401

  • scope: "selected" with one cid sets that tour public or hidden
  • scope: "all" sets every tour on the account public or hidden
  • scope missing, or selected with an empty or absent cids, returns 400 and writes nothing
  • The all path ignores any search or paging state
  • The all path completes in reasonable time for a 500-tour account, as one operation
  • A cid belonging to another account is never written — every query is scoped by user_id
  • The column is written as a string ("0" / "1"), matching how existing readers compare it
  • The response carries the summary block reflecting the state after the change
  • Failure returns a clear message the frontend can show

• Endpoint: POST /tours/ai-blur — existing route, new optional request field

  "panos": [101, 102],
  "userId": 55,
  "moderationId": 900,
  "aiBlurBudget": 2,
  "type": "face",
  "saveOnly": false
}

{

issues.display_title: Issue #1716: feat(panoramas): enforce Pro/Agency subscription on POST /panoramas/change-placeid
issues.main_description_html:
What

POST /panoramas/change-placeid (Edit Pano Place ID on the dashboard's Edit Panorama page) is being restricted to Pro and Agency subscribers.

The dashboard side is covered by GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4165, but that gate is UI-only and trivially bypassable. The API has to enforce it too.

Current state

  • The route is registered outside the auth middleware group in routes/panoramaRoutes.php.
  • Because of that, ChangePanoPlaceIdController reads user_id straight from the request body instead of the token.
  • ChangePanoPlaceIdAction only checks moderation ownership. No subscription check at all.

⚠️ Please verify first: the dashboard never sends user_id in the body, so the ownership check may currently be receiving 0 and rejecting every legitimate request. If that's the case, this task also fixes a live bug — confirm the actual behaviour on staging/production before starting.

Requested changes

  1. Move the route into the auth middleware group so user_id and subscribtion come from the verified token, not from client input.
  2. In the action, after the ownership check, reject the request when the user is not on a Pro or Agency plan.
  3. Allowed plans: Pro (1), Pro Yearly (6), Agency (5), Agency Yearly (8), Sub-account (4).

    ❓ Confirm whether Sub-account should be allowed. The dashboard task assumes yes.

  4. Return a clear domain error for the rejection (new domain code + HTTP status), consistent with how the other panorama exceptions are handled. Don't reuse PANORAMA.NOT_OWNER — the reason is different.
  5. Add the error message to the translation files.

Notes

  • App\Helpers\Tours\SubscriptionHelper already exists but its list is "any active paid plan" (includes Basic). Pro/Agency is a different, narrower set — add a separate method rather than changing the existing one, since other actions depend on it.
  • Update the endpoint docs (docs/v2/panoramas/change-placeid.md) — auth requirement, new error row, and the fact that user_id is no longer a body field.

Done when

  • Request without a valid token → 401.
  • Pro / Agency / Sub-account user, owns the tour → Place ID updates as before.
  • Basic or pay-as-you-go user, owns the tour → rejected with the new subscription error, Place ID unchanged.
  • Sending someone else's user_id in the body has no effect — identity comes from the token only.
  • Dashboard's existing call still works unchanged for eligible users.
  • Docs updated.

Related

  • Frontend: GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4165

Dev Note — After Implementation

Done in PR #1719.

  • The suspected live bug is confirmed. The route sat outside auth, the dashboard sends no user_id, so userId resolved to 0 and checkModerationOwnership(0, $mid) rejected every legitimate request with NOT_OWNER. Traced the origin: the legacy handler did its own checkToken() / userDatas($token), and the ADR migration in 498053179 (22 Jun) dropped that without moving the route into the auth group. It was simultaneously an IDOR for any caller that did send user_id.
  • Route moved into the auth group. The controller reads identity with $request->input(), not $request->user_id: the magic property resolves through all(), which is array_replace_recursive(input(), allFiles()) — files win — so an uploaded part named user_id could shadow the merged token value. input() never consults allFiles().
  • SubscriptionHelper::isProOrAgencySubscription() added for [1, 4, 5, 6, 8], separate from isActiveSubscription(). Sub-account included as confirmed. Known limitation now documented in the helper: code 4 is self-certifying — a sub-account whose parent org downgrades to Basic keeps subscribtion = 4 and stays eligible.
  • New PanoramaSubscriptionNotAllowedException → PANORAMA.SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_ALLOWED → 403. Ownership is checked before the plan, so a non-owner cannot use the endpoint to probe plan state.
  • No new translation key. messages.validation.subscription_not_allowed already carried the exact wording, so the exception reuses it rather than adding a panorama-specific copy to every locale. It was present in 18 of 19 locales — added the missing id translation.
  • 44 tests passing, including a new controller test proving body/query user_id and subscribtion cannot override the token, and that an uploaded part named user_id cannot shadow it. Endpoint docs and REGISTERED_APIS.md synced.

issues.display_title: Issue #1730: fix(paypal): refund the capture when one-time fulfilment fails
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

When a one-time order is captured and fulfilment then fails, the payment stays with us and the customer gets nothing. This is not caused by the customer — ownership checks, billing lookups and validation all run after the money is taken.

The subscription path already handles this. SubscribeHandler.php:205 calls refundCapture() on a post-capture failure and logs it:

if ($captureId) {
    try {
        $this->captureSubscription->refundCapture($captureId, $error->getMessage(), $isTestMode);
    } catch (\Exception $refundError) {
        error_log("Refund failed for capture {$captureId}: " . $refundError->getMessage());
    }
}

refundCapture() lives in CaptureSubscription.php:351 and uses the same PaypalHelper. The one-time order path never calls it.

Separately, there is no database transaction anywhere in app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/OneTimePayment/ (grep -rn "beginTransaction\|DB::transaction" returns nothing). Each process*Success() performs several writes in sequence — unlock, invoice, CCTrans, CCLog, email — so a failure partway through can leave an unlock with no invoice, or an invoice with no unlock. Reordering validation before capture does not close this: the PayPal call can succeed and a later database write can still fail.

Change

  • Call refundCapture() from the one-time order capture error path, mirroring SubscribeHandler. Extract it somewhere both paths can use rather than duplicating.
  • Wrap the writes inside each process*Success() in a database transaction so fulfilment is all-or-nothing.
  • If the refund itself fails, record it — that is the only trace left of a payment nobody can reconcile.

Acceptance

  • Post-capture fulfilment failures now return a localized support message instead of exposing the internal exception.
  • Added fulfilment_failed_contact_support translations for all locale files.

issues.display_title: Issue #1728: fix(paypal): bind the captured order to the product it was priced for
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

PayPal locks a payment amount at order creation (POST /paypal/orders), but the capture endpoints recompute the price/product from the request body and fulfil it without ever comparing against what was actually locked. Nothing binds a paid order to the product it was created for.

  • Overlay period. Create defaults period to 1 (dashboard never sends it), price is cost * period, but capture unlocks whatever period the body carries. Paid $20, granted a $100 five-year unlock — on ordinary checkouts, no abuse needed.
  • Product substitution. Capture routes on the product_name in the request body, not on what the order was created for. Buy the cheapest token pack, capture it as an overlay unlock.
  • Public overlay endpoints. Same gap, no auth required — /paypal/orders/capture-overlay bounds period, /paypal/overlay-orders (create) doesn't validate it at all.

Change

  • Validate-and-price before capturing (CaptureOrder restructured to match CaptureOverlayOrder's existing order).
  • Compare the recomputed total (and, on a Redis cache hit, the product_name) against the order's PayPal-locked amount. Reject with 409 before any capture call on a mismatch.
  • Bound period to 1-5 in the single helper method shared by all four create/capture endpoints.
  • CreateOrder caches the locked total + product name in Redis right after order creation (fast path); getOrderDetails() stays the authoritative PayPal fallback on a cache miss.
  • CreateOverlayOrder.php intentionally not touched — the dashboard doesn't send period at create time, so adding a required rule there would break the live public-overlay-create flow.

total_pano-driven blue-line pricing is a related but distinct exposure (client-supplied value sent consistently to both endpoints, so this comparison can't catch it) — closed separately in #1732.

issues.main_description_html:
Background

Currently, when a user downgrades their subscription plan, the system still creates a purchase record and generates an invoice for that downgrade — even though no payment is actually charged at that moment.

Going forward, invoice for downgrade will not be generated at the moment the user downgrades anymore. Instead, it will be generated later by a cronjob (to be built in a follow-up task).

Goal

Downgrade action should no longer generate a purchase record or invoice. A downgrade is a plan change, not a payment event, so it shouldn't produce an invoice.

Scope for this task

  • Applies to Stripe downgrade only.
  • Enabled for test users only (not rolled out to all users yet).

DowngradeHelper::insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade() gained a $deferInvoice param. issues.display_title: Issue #1752: Remove legacy SubscriptionClass dependency from Stripe subs complete-3ds
issues.main_description_html:
Why

POST /v2/payment/subscription/complete-3ds (Stripe subs 3DS completion) is the only remaining live caller of legacy SubscriptionClass::completeSubs3DS() (app/Class/Payment/SubscriptionClass.php:506). The /subs step itself (Subscription.php) already uses the modern action-class pattern — this is the one piece of the subs flow still routed through the legacy class.

Problem found during review

  • completeSubs3DS() rebuilds a bare (object)['id' => $subsId] stub from the Redis-stashed data and writes users / user_extra_data / cc_purchase as a successful payment unconditionally — there is no status === 'paid' check anywhere in this path.
  • Compare the sibling flow CompleteUpgrade3DS.php:98-102, which retrieves the live subscription + invoice from Stripe and throws unless status === 'paid'. Subs' 3DS-complete has no equivalent guard.
  • FE (useSubscribe.jsx) does gate on paymentIntent.status === 'succeeded' before calling this endpoint, but the backend has no independent verification of its own. A direct call to /complete-3ds with a valid-but-unconfirmed client_secret returned by step 1 would activate the subscription and write a success purchase record without payment ever completing.
  • The one Stripe call that does exist in this path (resolveStripeSubscriptionBillingInterval()) only fetches a billing-interval label for logging, and its catch (ApiErrorException) swallows failures and returns null — completion proceeds regardless, so it can't double as the verification step.

Scope

  • Replace the SubscriptionClass::completeSubs3DS() call in CompleteSubs3DS.php with a modern implementation, following the CompleteUpgrade3DS.php pattern:
    • Retrieve the live subscription + latest_invoice from Stripe
    • Verify the invoice is actually paid before writing anything
    • Move the finalize logic (user/plan update, cc_logs + cc_purchase insert, invoice, email) into the action class or a helper, matching how upgrade does it
  • Remove SubscriptionClass::completeSubs3DS() (and any private helper it alone used) once nothing calls it

Out of scope (separate work)

  • ch_ / invoice_id population on cc_purchase — column tracked in #1751, extraction logic is a follow-up once this endpoint has a real invoice object to read from
  • /subs sync path, /upgrade, /downgrade, /space-addon — not touched here
  • The other dead new SubscriptionClass() instantiations in GetSubStatus.php, CalculateProration.php, SubscriptionController.php (constructed, never called) — cleanup, not correctness, can be its own small PR

  • /complete-3ds rejects finalization when Stripe reports the invoice isn't paid (mirrors upgrade's behavior)

issues.display_title: Issue #1754: Standardize Stripe transid to charge id (ch_) in cc_logs and cc_purchase
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Standardize transid in cc_logs and cc_purchase to the Stripe charge id (ch_...) for Stripe payments, across the subscribe and subscribe-3ds flows.

Current state

For subscriptions created via POST /v2/payment/subscription/subs and completed via POST /v2/payment/subscription/complete-3ds (SubscriptionHelpers::handlePaymentSuccess()), transid is populated inconsistently:

  • cc_logs.transid = Stripe customer id (cus_...) — set in SubscriptionHelpers::logPaymentSuccess().
  • cc_purchase.transid = Stripe subscription id (sub_..., recurring) or PaymentIntent id (pi_..., one-time) — set in SubscriptionHelpers::generateAndSaveInvoice() → CCTransClass::insert().

Neither matches InvoiceHelper::classifyPaymentProcessorByTransId(), which only recognizes the legacy ch_(1|3)... charge-id shape — so every row from this flow classifies as unrecognized_format, and the Stripe product-lookup fallback (applyStripeProductFilter()) that depends on that classification never fires for new rows.

The receipt/invoice lookup path (InvoiceHelper::normalizeTransactionId(), findPurchaseByTransaction()) already assumes a ch_-prefixed id — it strips the ch_ prefix and matches either form. That code was written for charge ids; the subscribe flow just never supplied one.

Target state

Both cc_logs.transid and cc_purchase.transid store the Stripe charge id (ch_...) for Stripe payments, resolved from:

  • Recurring subscriptions: the charge behind invoice.payment_intent.latest_charge (needs an extra expand level beyond the current latest_invoice.payment_intent).
  • One-time payments: paymentIntent.latest_charge (needs expand: ['latest_charge'] on paymentIntents->create()).

Same expand additions are needed on the 3DS resume path, which re-retrieves the subscription/invoice/PaymentIntent from Stripe before finalizing (CompleteSubs3DS::handle()).

Scope

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Subscription/SubscriptionHelpers.php
    • logPaymentSuccess() — write charge id instead of customer->id to cc_logs.TransID.
    • generateAndSaveInvoice() — write charge id instead of subsId to cc_purchase.transid.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/Subscription/Subscription.php
    • createStripeCustomerAndSubscription() — add expand for the charge on both the subscription and one-time payment intent creation calls.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/Subscription/CompleteSubs3DS.php
    • handle() — add the same expand on the subscription/invoice and PaymentIntent retrieve calls used to verify the 3DS result.

Out of scope

  • No backfill/migration of existing cc_logs/cc_purchase rows.
  • No changes to Upgrade, Downgrade, PayPal subscribe, or one-time non-subscription purchase flows — none of them write customer->id/subsId into transid.
  • No changes to subscription lifecycle code (cancel/upgrade/downgrade/proration) — that reads user_extra_data.recurring_profile, a separate column, not cc_purchase.transid.

issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Same class of problem as #1754, on the PayPal side: cc_logs.transid and cc_purchase.transid hold two different PayPal entity ids for PayPal subscribe payments, and the recurring path discards a capture id it already fetched.

Current state

SubscribeHandler.php (app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/SubscribeHandler.php) builds a mock $subscribe object and calls the same SubscriptionHelpers::handlePaymentSuccess() used by the Stripe flow. ChargeIdResolver::resolve() (added in #1754) correctly returns null for this PayPal-shaped object (it has no Stripe latest_invoice/latest_charge fields), so PayPal keeps its pre-#1754 behavior untouched — which has the same mismatch #1754 fixed for Stripe:

  • cc_logs.transid = customer->id = PayPal payer_id (logPaymentSuccess(), unchanged by #1754).
  • cc_purchase.transid = subsId = $subscribe->id, which is:
    • One-time (SubscribeHandler.php:140-146): $captureId ?? $transactionId — the PayPal capture id if available, else the order/transaction id. This is already close to right (capture id is PayPal's rough equivalent of a Stripe charge id).
    • Recurring (SubscribeHandler.php:152-176): the PayPal subscription id (I-...). A capture id IS fetched a few lines earlier ($captureId = $transaction['resource_id'] ?? null;, line 155) but is discarded for this purpose — it's only used later for refund calls in the error-handling catch block (lines 206-211), never for $subscribe->id.

Same downstream consequence as #1754: cc_logs.transid and cc_purchase.transid can't be joined on transid directly, and neither matches InvoiceHelper::classifyPaymentProcessorByTransId()'s recognized shapes (it has no PayPal capture-id pattern at all, only PayPal Express/Payflow legacy patterns — see InvoiceHelper.php:280-307).

Target state

To be designed (this issue is filed to track investigation + design, not scoped yet). Candidate direction based on #1754's approach: resolve a single PayPal capture id once per successful payment and write it to both cc_logs.transid and cc_purchase.transid, with the recurring path using the $captureId it already fetches instead of discarding it. Needs design discussion on:

  • Whether capture_id is reliably available for recurring subscriptions on first payment (the try/catch around getSubscriptionTransactions() in SubscribeHandler.php:153-160 suggests it isn't always).
  • Fallback behavior when no capture id is available, analogous to #1754's 100%-off-coupon fallback case.
  • Whether classifyPaymentProcessorByTransId() needs a new pattern branch for PayPal capture ids, or whether that's out of scope like it was for #1754's Stripe charge ids.

Out of scope (for this filing)

  • Not implementing anything yet — investigation/design only, follow the same brainstorming → spec → plan flow used for #1754 when picked up.
  • CaptureOrder.php / CaptureOverlayOrder.php (PayPal one-time non-subscription purchases) are a separate code path (PaymentHelpers::logSuccessPayment / LogSuccessPayment DTO) not covered by this investigation.

issues.display_title: Issue #1766: Use PayPal capture id as transid for upgrade flow
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

PayPal subscription upgrade still stores the new PayPal subscription id (I-...) as transid in payment artifacts.

Current upgrade path:

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/UpgradeHandler.php
    • postUpdateBestEffort() calls insertCCPurchaseForUpgrade(transactionId: $newSubscription['id'] ?? '', ...)
    • upgrade success email uses subs_transaction_id => $newSubscription['id'] ?? ''

That means cc_logs.transid, cc_purchase.transid, invoice lookup, and email transaction id use the subscription id instead of the actual PayPal capture/transaction id.

Reference

Use PayPal subscription flow as reference:

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/SubscribeHandler.php
    • recurring path calls getSubscriptionTransactions($transactionId, $isTestMode)
    • stores latest transaction id as $captureId
    • builds subscribe object with id => $transactionId and capture_id => $captureId
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Subscription/PaypalTransIdResolver.php
    • returns $subscribe->capture_id ?? $subscribe->id ?? null

So user recurring profile should still use the PayPal subscription id (I-...), but payment transaction records should prefer the PayPal capture/transaction id when available.

Expected

PayPal upgrade should keep I-... only as the recurring subscription/profile id, but use the latest PayPal capture/transaction id as transid when writing payment artifacts:

  • cc_logs.transid
  • cc_purchase.transid
  • generated invoice lookup/id
  • upgrade success email subs_transaction_id
